target.title: fix(ui): Realtime Talk hangs when Google Live connections stall
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI users starting Realtime Talk with Google Live could remain stuck in the connecting state when the browser WebSocket never opened or opened without Google ever completing protocol setup. During that stall, the microphone, camera stream, input meter, and both audio contexts could remain active indefinitely. A socket error or close before readiness could leave the same resources active until the user manually dismissed the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser WebSocket construction has no caller-configurable startup deadline, so the Google Live transport now owns a 30-second deadline covering the full startup phase through the current socket's Google `setupComplete` frame. This matches the existing Realtime Talk WebRTC setup deadline while using the provider-specific readiness signal instead of treating the lower-level WebSocket `open` event as ready.

Timeout, error, and close paths report the transport error and stop the current socket lifecycle exactly once. Captured-socket checks before and after asynchronous message decoding keep stale socket events from clearing a replacement attempt's timer or emitting readiness for it. The conflict resolution with the merged Gemini Live video work preserves camera-frame shutdown, media-track release, and `onVideoStream(null)` cleanup.

## User Impact

Google Live Realtime Talk now fails with a clear error instead of connecting forever when either the WebSocket handshake or Google protocol setup stalls. Failed, closed, and timed-out attempts release the microphone, camera, input meter, socket, and both AudioContext instances without waiting for another user action.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3614ee6fa9287672c58763ffeecb048819a59f9c`, based on `8020dd3e0830ead01dc81c8a446444078315b63d`. The branch was rebuilt from current `main` using only the two substantive PR commits, removing two historical merge commits and resolving the sole conflict with #109719's video lifecycle.

- Node 24.15.0 focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-google-live.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-google-live-video.test.ts` - 2 files and 28 tests passed.
- Regression coverage proves both pre-open and post-open/no-`setupComplete` timeout paths. The video-enabled path verifies audio and camera tracks stop, the socket closes, and `onVideoStream` receives `null` after the combined stream.
- A separate regression proves that the current socket's `setupComplete` frame clears the deadline and emits `listening`, so a healthy session is not timed out later.
- Existing terminal-path coverage verifies `error -> close`, direct pre-open `close`, and manual stop release resources and clear timers once.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. Stable patch ID after the final rebase: `74ccb1db30be21ec23a1414f6568aa584fb8044a`.
- Bounded live observation against Google's documented constrained WebSocket endpoint with an intentionally invalid probe token: `{"reason":"watchdog","elapsedMs":15060,"readyState":2,"events":[{"type":"open","ms":812}]}`. It establishes the specific post-open/no-application-readiness state now bounded by the patch.
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review of the rebuilt exact patch found no P1/P2 issue and judged the timeout plus video cleanup conflict resolution correct after checking the full transport, callers, siblings, current-main video behavior, and both focused suites.

Proof gap: the live probe was not an authenticated Google Live success session. This environment has no `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` and cannot provide redacted real-browser proof of the patched visible error and media/context cleanup, so that remains for a credentialed browser run or maintainer review. The focused tests exercise those exact cleanup effects deterministically.

Remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment, so the focused Node 24 run used the repository's allowed local fallback.

AI-assisted: yes (Codex). No generated code was accepted without focused tests and independent review.
